claims.subject: Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting
claims.evidence_quote: Consider a complete network of n processors with at least ⌈αn⌉ non-faulty processors and CONGEST communication model.

claims.subject: Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting
claims.evidence_quote: Then there is a Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting (FTDTC) algorithm which raises an alert when the triggers received by the non-faulty processors are w in O(n log2 n log w∕α2) messages with high probability.

claims.subject: Explicit Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting
claims.evidence_quote: Input: A complete n processor anonymous network where at least ⌈αn⌉ processors are non-faulty, where α is a real number in the range [ln2 n∕n, 1].

claims.subject: candidate processor
claims.evidence_quote: Each candidate processor u informs other processors about their candidature. All the candidate processors form a committee.

claims.subject: committee processors
claims.evidence_quote: In the case of phase 2, whenever a processor receives the trigger, the processor sends the message to the committee processors and the committee processors further send the message to all the committee processors (if not sent earlier), which requires O(n(ln n∕α)2) messages.

claims.subject: Each processor computes a threshold value
claims.evidence_quote: Each processor computes a threshold value τ = ⌊ w12n⌋.
